people.name: Warren Hastings
people.summary: First Governor-General of Bengal (1773–85) under the Regulating Act.

roles.title: Governor-General of Bengal
roles.appointedBy: British Parliament — named in the Regulating Act, 1773
roles.howEnded: resigned in 1785; later impeached and acquitted

facts: Ended the Dual Government of Bengal in 1772 and moved the treasury from Murshidabad to Calcutta.
Introduced the Quinquennial (five-year) land settlement in 1772, later changed to annual settlement in 1776.
Set up district Diwani (civil) and Faujdari (criminal) Adalats in 1772.
Founded the Calcutta Madrasa in 1781 and supported William Jones's Asiatic Society of Bengal (1784).
The Pitt's India Act (1784) was passed during his tenure.
Fought the First Anglo-Maratha War (ended by the Treaty of Salbai, 1782) and the Second Anglo-Mysore War (ended by the Treaty of Mangalore, 1784).
Rohilla War (1774) fought with Awadh against the Rohillas.
Impeached in Britain on his return (1787–95), led by Edmund Burke; acquitted in 1795.
Nanda Kumar was tried and hanged (1775) during his rule — a charge in his impeachment.
people.source: Spectrum (Rajiv Ahir) / NCERT Modern India — standard chronology

people.name: Lord Cornwallis
people.summary: Governor-General 1786–93 (and briefly 1805); known for the Permanent Settlement and the Cornwallis Code.
titles: Father of the Indian Civil Service
facts: Introduced the Permanent Settlement (Zamindari system) in Bengal and Bihar in 1793.
The Cornwallis Code (1793) separated revenue administration from the judiciary.
Reorganised the civil service and banned private trade by Company servants; raised their salaries.
Created a graded system of courts: district courts up to the Sadar Diwani Adalat.
Third Anglo-Mysore War (1790–92) was ended by the Treaty of Seringapatam (1792); Tipu ceded half his kingdom.
Had earlier surrendered to the Americans at Yorktown (1781).
Died at Ghazipur in October 1805 during his second term.

people.name: Sir John Shore
people.summary: Governor-General 1793–98; followed a policy of non-intervention.
facts: Followed a policy of non-intervention in the affairs of Indian states.
Battle of Kharda (1795) between the Nizam and the Marathas took place in his time; the British did not help the Nizam.
Charter Act of 1793 was passed just as his term began.
Played a major role in planning the Permanent Settlement under Cornwallis.

people.name: Lord Wellesley
people.summary: Governor-General 1798–1805; expanded British power through the Subsidiary Alliance.
facts: Introduced the Subsidiary Alliance system in 1798.
The Nizam of Hyderabad was the first to accept the Subsidiary Alliance (1798).
Other states that accepted it: Mysore (1799), Tanjore (1799), Awadh (1801), the Peshwa (1802, Treaty of Bassein), Bhonsle (1803), Scindia (1803).
Fourth Anglo-Mysore War (1799): Tipu Sultan was killed defending Seringapatam.
Second Anglo-Maratha War (1803–05) followed the Treaty of Bassein (1802).
Founded the Fort William College at Calcutta (1800) to train Company civil servants.
Passed the Censorship of the Press Act, 1799.

pairs.right: Peshwa Baji Rao II & the British

people.name: Sir George Barlow
facts: The Vellore Mutiny (1806) of Indian sepoys took place during his tenure.

images.credit: Sir_George_Barlow,_1st_Bt_from_NPG.jpg: unknown artist derivative work: Beao / Wikimedia Commons

people.name: Lord Minto I
facts: Concluded the Treaty of Amritsar (1809) with Maharaja Ranjit Singh, fixing the Sutlej as the boundary.
Charter Act of 1813 was passed at the end of his term.

people.name: Lord Hastings
people.summary: Governor-General 1813–23; ended Maratha power and adopted a policy of intervention and war.
facts: Started the policy of "paramountcy": the Company claimed its authority was supreme over Indian states.
Anglo-Nepal War (1814–16) ended with the Treaty of Sugauli (1816).
Third Anglo-Maratha War (1817–19) ended the Peshwa's office; Baji Rao II was pensioned off to Bithur.
Suppressed the Pindaris (1817–19).
The Paika uprising of Khurda (1817) broke out in his time (NCERT).

people.name: Lord Amherst
facts: First Anglo-Burmese War (1824–26) ended with the Treaty of Yandabo (1826); Assam came under British control.
Barrackpore Mutiny (1824) of sepoys who refused to go to Burma.

people.name: Lord William Bentinck
people.summary: Last GG of Bengal (1828–33) and first GG of India (1833–35); a social reformer.
facts: Abolished Sati by Regulation XVII of 1829, with support from Raja Ram Mohan Roy.
Suppressed Thuggee with the help of William Sleeman.
English Education Act 1835 followed Macaulay's Minute (1835), making English the medium of higher education.
Annexed Mysore (1831), Coorg (1834) and Central Cachar (1834).
Charter Act 1833 made him the first Governor-General of India.
Was Governor of Madras at the time of the Vellore Mutiny (1806) and was recalled.
Calcutta Medical College founded in 1835.

images.credit: Based on painting by Sir T. Lawrence (1769 – 1s830) / Wikimedia Commons

people.name: Sir Charles Metcalfe
facts: Removed restrictions on the press by the Press Act of 1835.
Earlier negotiated the Treaty of Amritsar (1809) with Ranjit Singh as an envoy.

people.name: Lord Auckland
people.summary: Governor-General 1836–42; started the First Anglo-Afghan War.
facts: Signed the Tripartite Treaty (1838) with Ranjit Singh and Shah Shuja.
First Anglo-Afghan War (1839–42) ended in a disastrous British retreat from Kabul.

people.name: Lord Ellenborough
facts: Ended the First Anglo-Afghan War (1842).
Sindh was annexed in 1843 by Charles Napier.
Slavery was abolished in India by Act V of 1843.

people.name: Lord Hardinge I
facts: First Anglo-Sikh War (1845–46) ended with the Treaty of Lahore (1846).
Treaty of Amritsar (1846) sold Kashmir to Gulab Singh.
Banned female infanticide and human sacrifice among the Gonds.

images.credit: After Francis Holl / Eden Upton Eddis / Wikimedia Commons

people.name: Lord Dalhousie
people.summary: Governor-General 1848–56; annexation through the Doctrine of Lapse and modernisation.
facts: Doctrine of Lapse annexed Satara (1848), Sambalpur (1850), Udaipur (1852), Nagpur (1853) and Jhansi (1854) (NCERT).
Awadh was annexed in 1856 on grounds of misrule, not lapse (NCERT).
Second Anglo-Sikh War (1848–49) led to the annexation of Punjab (1849).
Second Anglo-Burmese War (1852) annexed Lower Burma (Pegu).
First railway line, Bombay–Thane, opened on 16 April 1853.
First telegraph line (Calcutta–Agra) and the Post Office Act 1854.
Wood's Despatch (1854) — the 'Magna Carta of English education in India'.
Widow Remarriage Act (1856) was passed just after he left (under Canning).
Public Works Department set up.

people.name: Lord Canning
people.summary: Last GG under the Company (1856–58) and first Viceroy (1858–62).
facts: The Revolt of 1857 broke out during his tenure.
Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act 1856 was passed in his time.
Universities of Calcutta, Bombay and Madras were founded in 1857.
Queen Victoria's Proclamation was read by him at Allahabad on 1 November 1858.
Indian Councils Act 1861 and the Indian Penal Code (1860) came in his time.
Withdrew the Doctrine of Lapse.

images.credit: John Jabez Edwin Mayall / Wikimedia Commons

people.name: Lord Elgin I
people.summary: Viceroy 1862–63; died in office at Dharamsala.
facts: Suppressed the Wahabi movement.
Died at Dharamsala in 1863.

people.name: Sir John Lawrence
facts: Followed a policy of 'Masterly Inactivity' towards Afghanistan.
Bhutan War (1865).
High Courts set up at Calcutta, Bombay and Madras (1865).
Set up the Indian Forest Department (1864).

people.name: Lord Mayo
facts: Began financial decentralisation (1870) — the start of provincial finance.
First census of India was attempted in 1872 (non-synchronous).
Founded Mayo College at Ajmer (1872) for the sons of princes.
Set up the Statistical Survey of India.
Only Viceroy murdered in office — killed by Sher Ali Afridi at Port Blair (1872).

people.name: Lord Northbrook
facts: Kuka movement in Punjab took place in his time.
The Prince of Wales (later Edward VII) visited India in 1875.

people.name: Lord Lytton
facts: Held the Delhi Durbar of 1877 proclaiming Queen Victoria 'Kaiser-i-Hind' (Empress of India) — during the Great Famine (1876–78).
Vernacular Press Act, 1878 — the 'Gagging Act'.
Arms Act, 1878 required Indians to hold a licence for arms.
Lowered the maximum age for the ICS exam from 21 to 19 (1876).
Second Anglo-Afghan War (1878–80).
Set up the Famine Commission under Richard Strachey (1878).

people.name: Lord Ripon
titles: Father of Local Self-Government in India
facts: Resolution on Local Self-Government (1882).
Repealed the Vernacular Press Act (1882).
First Factory Act (1881) to improve working conditions.
First regular (synchronous) census in 1881.
Hunter Commission on education (1882).
Ilbert Bill controversy (1883–84): Indian judges trying Europeans.

images.credit: London Stereoscopic & Photographic Company / Wikimedia Commons

people.name: Lord Dufferin
people.summary: Viceroy 1884–88; the INC was founded in his time.
facts: Indian National Congress was founded in 1885.
Third Anglo-Burmese War (1885) — Upper Burma annexed (1886).
Called the Congress a 'microscopic minority'.
people.wiki: Frederick Hamilton-Temple-Blackwood, 1st Marquess of Dufferin and Ava

images.credit: The Notman studio, Ottawa William J. Topley, proprietor / Wikimedia Commons

people.name: Lord Lansdowne
facts: Durand Line (1893) drawn between British India and Afghanistan by Sir Mortimer Durand.
Indian Councils Act, 1892 introduced indirect election.
Age of Consent Act, 1891 raised the age of consent for girls to 12.

people.name: Lord Elgin II
facts: Great famine of 1896–97; Lyall Commission appointed.
Chapekar brothers assassinated plague officials Rand and Ayerst at Poona (1897).

people.name: Lord Curzon
facts: Partition of Bengal announced July 1905, effective 16 October 1905.
Indian Universities Act, 1904 (after the Raleigh Commission, 1902).
Ancient Monuments Preservation Act, 1904; revived the Archaeological Survey of India under John Marshall.
Police Commission under Andrew Fraser (1902).
Created the North-West Frontier Province (1901).
Younghusband expedition to Tibet (1903–04).
Calcutta Corporation Act, 1899 reduced elected members.
Resigned after a dispute with Lord Kitchener, the Commander-in-Chief.
people.wiki: George Curzon, 1st Marquess Curzon of Kedleston

images.credit: George Grantham Bain Collection (Library of Congress) / Wikimedia Commons

people.name: Lord Minto II
facts: Muslim League founded at Dacca (1906).
Surat Split of the Congress (1907).
Indian Councils Act, 1909 (Morley–Minto Reforms) introduced separate electorates for Muslims.
Received the Simla Deputation led by the Aga Khan (1906).

people.name: Lord Hardinge II
facts: Partition of Bengal annulled at the Delhi Durbar of 1911 (King George V).
Capital shifted from Calcutta to Delhi (announced 1911).
A bomb was thrown at him in Delhi (Delhi Conspiracy Case, 1912).
Hindu Mahasabha founded (1915) by Madan Mohan Malaviya.
people.wiki: Charles Hardinge, 1st Baron Hardinge of Penshurst

people.name: Lord Chelmsford
facts: Montagu–Chelmsford Reforms (Government of India Act 1919) introduced dyarchy in the provinces.
Rowlatt Act (1919) and the Jallianwala Bagh massacre (13 April 1919).
Hunter Committee appointed to inquire into Jallianwala Bagh.
Home Rule Leagues (1916) and the Lucknow Pact (1916).
Non-Cooperation and Khilafat movements began (1920).
Saddler Commission on education (1917).

people.name: Lord Reading
facts: Chauri Chaura incident (5 February 1922) led Gandhi to withdraw Non-Cooperation.
Moplah rebellion in Malabar (1921).
Swaraj Party formed (1923) by C.R. Das and Motilal Nehru.
Kakori train robbery (1925).
Repealed the Rowlatt Act and the Press Act of 1910.
RSS founded at Nagpur (1925) by K.B. Hedgewar.

people.name: Lord Irwin
facts: Simon Commission arrived in 1928 and was boycotted.
Irwin's 'Deepavali Declaration' (1929) promised Dominion Status as the goal.
Dandi March and Civil Disobedience (1930).
First Round Table Conference (1930).
Gandhi–Irwin Pact signed on 5 March 1931.
Butler Committee on Indian states (1927).
people.wiki: E. F. L. Wood, 1st Earl of Halifax

people.name: Lord Willingdon
facts: Second (1931) and Third (1932) Round Table Conferences.
Communal Award (1932) by Ramsay MacDonald.
Poona Pact (1932) between Gandhi and Ambedkar.
Government of India Act, 1935 passed.

people.name: Lord Linlithgow
facts: Provincial elections of 1937 under the 1935 Act; Congress ministries formed.
Congress ministries resigned in 1939 over India being dragged into World War II.
August Offer (1940).
Cripps Mission (1942).
Quit India Movement (August 1942).
Muslim League's Lahore Resolution (1940) demanding separate states.
Bengal famine of 1943 began in his time.

people.name: Lord Wavell
facts: Wavell Plan and the Simla Conference (1945).
INA trials at the Red Fort (1945).
Royal Indian Navy mutiny (1946).
Cabinet Mission (1946).
Direct Action Day (16 August 1946) called by the Muslim League.
Interim Government formed on 2 September 1946 under Nehru.

people.name: Lord Mountbatten
people.summary: Last Viceroy (Mar–Aug 1947) and first Governor-General of free India (1947–48).

roles.title: Governor-General of the Dominion of India

facts: Mountbatten Plan (3 June 1947) — partition of India.
Indian Independence Act, 1947 passed by the British Parliament.
Radcliffe Line drew the India–Pakistan border.
Brought forward the date of independence to 15 August 1947.
people.wiki: Louis Mountbatten, 1st Earl Mountbatten of Burma

people.name: C. Rajagopalachari
people.summary: Only Indian Governor-General (1948–50); proposed the C.R. Formula.

roles.title: Governor-General of the Dominion of India

facts: C.R. Formula (1944) proposed a plebiscite in Muslim-majority areas after the war.
Led the Vedaranyam salt march (1930) in Tamil Nadu.
First Indian and last Governor-General of India.
Founded the Swatantra Party (1959).
First recipient of the Bharat Ratna (1954), with S. Radhakrishnan and C.V. Raman.

images.credit: Gandhi_Rajagopalachari.jpg: Unknown authorUnknown author derivative work: Ganeshk (talk) / Wikimedia Commons

people.name: Dadabhai Naoroji
people.summary: Moderate leader and economist of the Drain Theory; INC president three times.

works.title: Poverty and Un-British Rule in India

facts: Put forward the Drain of Wealth theory.
First Indian elected to the British House of Commons (1892, Finsbury Central).
Declared Swaraj as the goal of the Congress at the Calcutta session (1906).
Founded the East India Association in London (1866).

pairs.left: Poverty and Un-British Rule in India

people.name: Gopal Krishna Gokhale
facts: Founded the Servants of India Society (1905).
Presided over the INC session at Benares (1905).
Gandhi called him his political guru.
Mahadev Govind Ranade was his mentor.

people.name: Annie Besant
people.summary: Theosophist and first woman INC president (1917); led a Home Rule League.
facts: Started the Home Rule League at Madras (Adyar) in September 1916.
Founded the Central Hindu College at Benares (1898), later part of BHU.
First woman president of the INC (Calcutta, 1917).
Led the Theosophical Society from Adyar, Madras.

people.name: Mahatma Gandhi
people.summary: Leader of the mass national movement through satyagraha and non-violence.

works.title: The Story of My Experiments with Truth

facts: Returned from South Africa on 9 January 1915 (now Pravasi Bharatiya Divas).
Champaran Satyagraha (1917) — his first satyagraha in India, for indigo farmers.
Ahmedabad mill strike (1918) — his first hunger strike in India.
Kheda Satyagraha (1918) for peasants hit by crop failure.
Led the Non-Cooperation Movement (1920–22) and withdrew it after Chauri Chaura.
Dandi March from Sabarmati, 12 March – 6 April 1930.
Attended only the Second Round Table Conference (1931).
Gave the call 'Do or Die' for Quit India (8 August 1942).
Presided over the INC only once — Belgaum, 1924.
Assassinated by Nathuram Godse on 30 January 1948.
Lived in South Africa 1893–1915; fought for Indian traders and indentured labour in Natal and Transvaal.
Attended the 2nd RTC (1931); led the CDM (Civil Disobedience Movement); Dandi March 12 Mar–6 Apr 1930.
Founded the All India Anti-Untouchability League (Harijan Sevak Sangh), 1932.
Assassinated 30 Jan 1948.
John Ruskin's "Unto This Last" deeply influenced him; he translated it into Gujarati as "Sarvodaya" (APPSC Group-1 key).
Influenced also by Tolstoy (The Kingdom of God is Within You).

people.name: Jawaharlal Nehru
people.summary: INC leader and first Prime Minister of India (1947–64).

roles.title: Prime Minister of India
roles.howGained: Leader of the Congress; head of the Interim Government (1946)

facts: Presided over the Lahore Congress (1929), which adopted Purna Swaraj.
Moved the Objectives Resolution in the Constituent Assembly (13 December 1946).
Headed the Interim Government (1946).
Gave the 'Tryst with Destiny' speech on the night of 14–15 August 1947.
Was both Prime Minister and Foreign Minister and shaped foreign policy from 1946 to 1964 (NCERT).
Announced the formation of Andhra State in December 1952 (NCERT).
Signed the Panchsheel with Zhou Enlai (1954) and the Indus Waters Treaty with Ayub Khan (1960) (NCERT).
A founder of the Non-Aligned Movement (Belgrade, 1961).

people.name: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel
people.summary: Led Bardoli Satyagraha; integrated the princely states as first Home Minister.

roles.title: Deputy Prime Minister and Home Minister

facts: Women of Bardoli gave him the title 'Sardar' (1928).
Presided over the Karachi Congress (1931), which passed the Fundamental Rights resolution.
Integrated over 560 princely states with V.P. Menon.
Police action ('Operation Polo', 1948) brought Hyderabad into India.
Called the 'Patron saint of India's civil servants'.
Statue of Unity in Gujarat honours him; 31 October is National Unity Day.
Wrote to princely rulers in 1947 urging accession (NCERT).
Died on 15 December 1950.
31 Oct is Rashtriya Ekta Diwas (National Unity Day).

images.credit: Government of India work / Wikimedia Commons

people.name: Subhas Chandra Bose
people.summary: INC president 1938–39; founded the Forward Bloc and led the INA.
facts: Resigned from the ICS in 1921.
Presided at Haripura (1938); defeated Pattabhi Sitaramayya at Tripuri (1939), then resigned.
Formed the Forward Bloc (1939).
Set up Azad Hind Radio in Germany and the Free India Legion.
Took charge of the INA in Singapore (1943); Provisional Government of Free India (21 October 1943).
Gave the slogans 'Jai Hind' and 'Delhi Chalo'.
C.R. Das was his political guru.
Formed the Azad Hind Govt 21 Oct 1943 Singapore; renamed Andaman "Shaheed" and Nicobar "Swaraj" (December 1943). In 2018 Neil and Havelock islands became Shaheed Dweep and Swaraj Dweep.
INA hoisted the flag at Moirang, Manipur (April 1944).
Said to have died in an air crash at Taihoku (Taiwan) on 18 Aug 1945.
23 January is Parakram Diwas; the INA trials defence team included Tej Bahadur Sapru, K.N. Katju and Bhulabhai Desai.

images.credit: Unknown (Netaji Research Bureau, Calcutta) / Wikimedia Commons
